nodes.name: Daily Schedule
nodes.notes: Starts the workflow on a timer — daily at 6:00. No input data; downstream nodes fetch what they need.

nodes.name: Read Source Feed
nodes.notes: Pulls the RSS feed and emits one item per entry (title, link, content). Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.name: Skip Already-Seen Posts
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.name: Keep Top Stories
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 5 items to protect downstream quotas.

nodes.name: Rewrite for Our Audience (AI)
nodes.notes: Single fixed LLM step (no tool choice) — cheaper and more predictable than an agent. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.name: OpenAI Chat Model
nodes.notes: Chat model powering the AI step (model: gpt-4o-mini). Swap providers here without rewiring. Credential: OpenAI API key. platform.openai.com → API keys → create new secret key.

nodes.name: Publish to Telegram
nodes.notes: Sends a Telegram message to the configured chat — the same bot can also receive replies, so this doubles as a two-way ops channel. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Telegram bot token. Message @BotFather on Telegram → /newbot → copy the token.

nodes.name: Publish to Slack
nodes.notes: Posts a message to Slack (#inbox-ops) — a low-latency way for the team to see automation activity without checking a dashboard. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Slack OAuth2. Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.

nodes.name: Confirm Cross-Post
nodes.notes: Rejoins 2 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Log Published Posts (Notion)
nodes.notes: Creates a new page in the Notion database — the title is pulled straight from the item's key field. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Notion integration token. notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.

nodes.name: Stamp Processing Time
nodes.notes: Stamps processedAt with the current time for auditing.

nodes.name: Save Execution Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Align Field Names
nodes.notes: Normalizes field names so every source feeds the same downstream schema.

nodes.name: Tag Pipeline Metadata
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes pipeline, version. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Summarize Run Stats
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes runAt, itemCount, status. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

# Deliver a metrics report: Telegram

**Pattern:** Scheduled Digest · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers drip-campaigns work end to end across Telegram, Notion and Slack.

It moves through 17 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. Daily Schedule
2. Read Source Feed
3. Skip Already-Seen Posts
4. Keep Top Stories
5. Rewrite for Our Audience (AI)
6. OpenAI Chat Model
7. Publish to Telegram
8. Publish to Slack
9. Confirm Cross-Post
10. Log Published Posts (Notion)
11. Stamp Processing Time
12. Save Execution Metadata
13. Align Field Names
14. Tag Pipeline Metadata
15. Summarize Run Stats
16. Append Audit Row (Notion)
17. Send Summary to Telegram

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Telegram — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing drip-campaigns work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Daily Schedule → Read Source Feed → Skip Already-Seen Posts → Keep Top Stories → Rewrite for Our Audience (AI) → OpenAI Chat Model → Publish to Telegram → Publish to Slack → Confirm Cross-Post → Log Published Posts (Notion) → Stamp Processing Time → Save Execution Metadata → Align Field Names → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Notion) → Send Summary to Telegram → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Telegram

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Telegram and Notion aligned by hand for drip campaigns
- Drip campaigns work where "Read Source Feed" is still a manual step before Telegram
- Drip campaigns work that only reaches Telegram on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Telegram and Notion in step for drip campaigns, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Telegram or Notion are skipped, across all 19 nodes of this drip-campaigns build
- A failed Telegram or Notion call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 19 nodes in this drip-campaigns build
- Every drip-campaigns run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Telegram
- The drip-campaigns AI step is isolated from Telegram, so models swap without touching the other 19 nodes

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Notion integration token; OpenAI API key; Slack OAuth2; Telegram bot token.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Deduplication is cross-execution, not just within a single run — an RSS feed re-serves the same items on every poll, and without this the same story would get posted again on every scheduled check.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Turn off the AI rewrite step and compare the raw feed text against the rewritten version.
2. Add a second RSS source and merge both into one feed before dedupe.
3. Change 'Keep Top Stories' from 5 to 1 and see how it changes posting cadence.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**OpenAI API key**
platform.openai.com → API keys → create new secret key.
_Gotcha:_ Needs billing set up; a brand-new key with no credit returns 429 immediately.

**Telegram bot token**
Message @BotFather on Telegram → /newbot → copy the token.
_Gotcha:_ Get your chat ID by messaging the bot then opening api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/getUpdates.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**Notion integration token**
notion.so/my-integrations → New integration → copy the Internal Integration Token.
_Gotcha:_ Then open the database → ••• → Connections → add your integration, or every call 404s.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your drip campaigns process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Telegram: the bot token is a bearer credential — rotate it if it ever appears in an execution log.
- Notion: share only the target database with the integration. An integration sees nothing you have not explicitly shared.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.

**Do not log**
drip-campaigns payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
